record.original_question: Classify all two-orbit 4-polytopes in hyperbolic 3-space H^3.

evidence.quote: Problem 30. Classify all two-orbit 4-polytopes in H^3.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A 4-polytope in hyperbolic 3-space $\mathbb{H}^3$ is a tessellation of $\mathbb{H}^3$ by 3-dimensional cells, regarded as an abstract polytope of rank 4 whose flags (maximal chains of faces) admit a faithful geometric realization in $\mathbb{H}^3$ via isometries. Let $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ denote the symmetry group of such a polytope $\mathcal{P}$, acting on the set $\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{P})$ of flags. The polytope $\mathcal{P}$ is called two-orbit if $\Gamma(\mathcal{P})$ acts on $\mathcal{F}(\mathcal{P})$ with exactly two orbits (in particular it is not flag-transitive). 

Problem: Classify, up to isometry of $\mathbb{H}^3$, all two-orbit 4-polytopes in $\mathbb{H}^3$, i.e. determine all such hyperbolic tessellations whose symmetry group has exactly two orbits on flags.
artifact.status_search_result: Web searches did not surface a classification of two-orbit 4-polytopes in hyperbolic 3-space. While related classifications (Coxeter polytopes, hyperideal polyhedra, regular hyperbolic honeycombs) exist, no source explicitly resolves the two-orbit case in $\mathbb{H}^3$, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Hyperbolic Coxeter Polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Lists known classifications of hyperbolic Coxeter polytopes but does not address two-orbit 4-polytopes in H^3.
status_evidence.claim: Related flag-transitive/Coxeter classifications exist, but the two-orbit case in H^3 is not listed as classified.

status_evidence.title: List of regular polytopes and compounds
status_evidence.snippet: Catalogs regular (one-orbit) hyperbolic honeycombs; no enumeration of two-orbit hyperbolic 4-polytopes is given.
status_evidence.claim: Only flag-transitive examples are catalogued in standard references.
